messages:
Sam P (PM): quick sync — we need a landing PRD + acceptance checklist for the embeddings SLOs before Monday. Customer P22 is pushing for predictable latency on hosted API. Can we agree on gating criteria and rollback triggers?
Alex W: do we have baseline numbers for current prod p95/p99?
Maria G: p95 ~ 180ms, p99 ~ 720ms for embeddings under normal 1k qps. those are from last week's telemetry.
Jon R: is the ask 99.9 availability or 99.9 p95? customer phrased it as '99.9 p95' which is ambiguous.
Sam P (PM): good call — Sam clarifies with customer, but planning assumption: they want p95 to be stable at target under typical traffic (not extreme bursts). we should draft both latency and error budget gating.
Eva S (SRE): proposal: acceptance requires p95 <= 200ms and error rate <= 0.2% over a 1h sliding window during canary. p99 < 1s as a softer guard. if either breaches for 15m, auto-roll back.
Alex W: sounds reasonable. Add KV cache miss scenarios — when cache cold p95 spikes. we should require warm-cache benchmark in PRD.
Maria G: acceptance checklist items I propose:
- automated benchmark run (warm & cold)
- canary at 5% for 30m -> verify gates -> ramp to 25% for 2h -> verify -> full rollout
- load test at 1.5x expected traffic
- latency histograms + error budget dashboard

Jon R: and add a fallback policy: if canary fails, route to quantized model or to Dedicated pool (if customer on Dedicated). That avoids full rollback for hosted.
Eva S (SRE): agree. fallback hierarchy: 1) light quantized model; 2) lower batch size / increase concurrency cap; 3) route to dedicated region; 4) rollback. each step needs a metric gate.
Sam P (PM): can we codify the gates? something like:```json
{
  "canary": {
    "p95_ms": 200,
    "error_rate_pct": 0.2,
    "duration_mins": 30
  },
  "ramp": {
    "p95_ms": 220,
    "error_rate_pct": 0.3,
    "duration_mins": 120
  }
}
```
Alex W: love the JSON. add tail-slo check: p99_ms < 1000 for both phases.
Maria G: edge cases: heavy batching jobs from clients, and tiny single-item inference spikes. need separate buckets in dashboards. also note cold-starts from short lived workers. add acceptance: startup latency tests.
Jon R: acceptance criteria bullet list for PRD (short form):
- functional correctness tests pass (unit + integration)
- benchmark: warm p95 <=200ms, warm p99 <1s; cold p95 <=400ms
- stability: canary gates pass as defined
- observability: dashboards + alerts + runbook present
- rollback policy + fallback chain documented

Eva S (SRE): alerting thresholds:
- Sev2 if p95 > 250ms for 30m
- Sev1 if p99 > 1.5s or error_rate > 1% for 10m
Also add synthetic tests for critical customers including P22.
Sam P (PM): rollout plan in PRD: timeline + owners + customer communication. who owns the canary checks?
Alex W: infra team owns automation. we'll add a lightweight canary-checker that posts results to #incidents and triggers rollout-bot.
rollout-bot: canary started: 5% -> monitoring p95/p99/error. (automated)
Maria G: docs: include 'how to reproduce' and 'how to force fallback' steps. keep them <1 page so ops can act fast.
Jon R: edge case: degraded model quality after quantization — need evaluation set and quality thresholds. acceptance must include QA on a small labeled prompt set (regression < 2% AUC drop or similar).
Sam P (PM): good call. add quality gate: model-level regression < 2% on P22 eval set during canary.
Eva S (SRE): last bit: add postmortem checklist if we roll back — timeline, signal, mitigation steps, customer notification template.
Sam P (PM): ok i'll draft the PRD with these bullets and post for review. next steps: alex + eva to sketch automation params, maria + jon to prepare benchmarks and eval harness. i'll aim to circulate draft by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:
